message.content:
This is the EGO Power+ Multi-Head System power head, and CBP has issued rulings on it. The classification question is whether it falls under 8701 (tractors), 8433 (other agricultural or horticultural machinery), 8467 (hand-held tools with self-contained motor), or 8432 (soil preparation machinery).

Walk-behind power heads that accept attachments are best compared to pedestrian-controlled tractors. Heading 8701 covers tractors, and 8701.10 covers pedestrian-controlled tractors. A pedestrian-controlled tractor is a wheeled unit that is walked behind and used to drive implements. In the 8701 explanatory notes, a tractor is a motor vehicle built mainly for hauling or pushing other machines, and a walk-behind power unit with a PTO that drives attachments fits that description.

In this case the power head delivers rotary force to attachments such as a tiller or cultivator. The 8701.10 subheading is "Pedestrian controlled tractors", and the 10-digit codes under it are 8701.10.0000 (the HTSUS has only 8701.10.00 with statistical suffixes). The 2022 HTSUS lists 8701.10.00 with a 10-digit breakdown: 8701.10.0000 for the base, covering pedestrian-controlled tractors. The duty rate is 2.5%.

The alternative is 8432.80 or 8433.60, but with the wheeled chassis, handles and drive function, 8701.10 is the better fit. I think CBP ruled this way for the EGO power head.

```json
{"hts_code": "8701.10.0000", "reason": "A battery-powered, wheeled walk-behind power head that drives interchangeable horticultural attachments is a pedestrian-controlled tractor of heading 8701, subheading 8701.10."}
```
